extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers, clinician-scientists, and grant applicants targeting NIH/clinical biomedical funding
extracted.subtask_description: Implicit rubric distilled from Eric Topol's Substack for what makes biomedical research worth funding: prioritizes translational impact, open-science practices, diverse cohorts, reproducibility, interpretable AI, and patient-centered outcomes. Useful for investigators preparing NIH/biomedical grant proposals or evaluating funding priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational impact within 5-10 years
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that affects clinical practice within 5-10 years is valued; 'bench to bedside' is the preferred framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with what the work means for patients/society; prioritize projects with a clear path to clinical implementation within a near-to-mid timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic science with clear clinical relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic science is valued when the path to clinical relevance is clear or when it has major breakthrough potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mechanistic/basic proposals, explicitly describe the downstream translational pathway and potential clinical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI/ML applications for clinical problems
rubrics_metrics.description: AI for diagnosis, drug discovery, multi-omic analysis, and foundation models in medicine are prioritized areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on clinically meaningful use-cases (diagnosis, therapeutics, prognostics); explain how AI advances lead to patient benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability and external validation for AI/ML
rubrics_metrics.description: Black-box AI without interpretability or external validation is penalized; interpretable models and external validation are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include model interpretability strategies, external validation cohorts, and benchmarking; avoid unsupported 'black-box' claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility through preregistration and open data/code
rubrics_metrics.description: Preregistration and open sharing of data and code are critical to address reproducibility concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregister analysis plans (OSF, ClinicalTrials.gov as appropriate); deposit code (e.g., GitHub) and data in appropriate repositories; describe reproducibility infrastructure in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-ancestry and diverse population inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Population diversity (multi-ancestry inclusion) is required to address past bias in genomics and other human studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide plans for diverse cohort recruitment, justify any single-ancestry focus, and describe analyses across ancestries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population-scale genomics and functional follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for population-scale genomics studies coupled with functional follow-up of GWAS hits and plans for clinical implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should combine large-scale discovery with concrete plans for experimental/functional validation and translation into clinical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-centered outcomes and partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient-reported outcomes, real-world evidence, decentralized trials, and patient partnership in study design are prioritized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include patient-centered endpoints, engagement strategies, and decentralized/real-world elements when appropriate; describe patient involvement in design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world evidence and decentralized trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies that incorporate real-world evidence and decentralized clinical trial designs are valued for patient relevance and scalability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe data sources, remote trial procedures, and how real-world data will be curated and validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication-oriented design and explicit replication goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Replication studies and designs that build replication into the project are encouraged; lack of replication is criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include replication cohorts or planned reproducibility checks; describe how results will be independently validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory preregistration of analysis plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-hoc analyses without pre-registration are penalized; preregistration of analysis plans is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify primary/secondary endpoints and analysis pipelines on OSF, ClinicalTrials.gov, or similar registries before data analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science as default (preprints, open peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open science practices (preprints for high-stakes findings, open peer review where possible) are advocated as norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post preprints for important results; consider open peer review options; be prepared to share materials publicly to accelerate scrutiny and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code on GitHub and data in appropriate repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Code should be available on platforms like GitHub and data deposited in appropriate repositories for transparency and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links or plans for data/code deposition in the application and maintain accessible repositories during and after the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative power calculations and effect-size estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Power analyses should use conservative effect-size assumptions to avoid underpowered studies and misleading claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify effect size assumptions, perform sensitivity analyses, and design studies with adequate power for realistic effect sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of hype language and unsupported grand claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of hyperbolic language ('revolutionary', 'paradigm-shifting') without strong evidence is penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State claims modestly and support them with data; clearly delineate speculation from demonstrated results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and management of conflicts of interest (COIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry funding and other COIs are legitimate but must be transparently disclosed and managed; lack of disclosure is penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominently disclose all COIs, describe safeguards (editorial firewalls, independent replication) and plans to mitigate bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid post-hoc subgroup analyses without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-hoc analyses and unplanned subgroup claims are penalized unless pre-specified or appropriately validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify subgroup analyses when possible; if exploratory, label them as such and plan validation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for smaller teams with clear accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller teams are sometimes preferred over mega-consortia when consortium structures dilute accountability; mega-consortia need clear PI responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing large consortia, specify leadership, accountability, decision-making, and reproducibility roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility infrastructure built into projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should include explicit reproducibility infrastructure (protocols, versioned code, data management) as part of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe workflows, version control, containerization, standardized pipelines, and QA/QC steps to ensure reproducible outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: External validation of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: External validation (independent cohorts, independent labs) is expected, particularly for high-impact or AI-driven claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for independent replication/validation cohorts and describe how external validation will be obtained and analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional experimental follow-up for genomic hits
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery of genomic associations should be paired with functional follow-up to demonstrate mechanism and translational relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experimental validation (in vitro, in vivo, or other assays) to link statistical associations to biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for clinical implementation in genomics
rubrics_metrics.description: Genomics proposals should include clear plans for clinical implementation and how findings will affect patient care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe clinical workflows, decision-support integration, and barriers to implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse cohort recruitment plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit plans to recruit diverse cohorts and address ancestry bias are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include recruitment strategies, community engagement plans, and analytic methods to handle diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient partnership in study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging patients as partners in research design and outcome selection is expected for patient-centered research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document patient advisory boards, co-design activities, and how patient input shaped endpoints and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world evidence integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporating real-world data and evidence streams strengthens clinical relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain data provenance, curation, linkage, and limitations of real-world sources; plan analyses to mitigate bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints for high-stakes findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints are expected for high-stakes or time-sensitive findings to accelerate dissemination and scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post to an appropriate preprint server and be ready to share underlying data/materials to support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistration on appropriate platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use OSF, ClinicalTrials.gov, or equivalent registries for preregistration depending on study type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registry identifiers in applications and ensure registries contain sufficient detail about endpoints and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code sharing from project start
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and share code (e.g., on GitHub) from project inception to demonstrate transparency and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use version control, document code, include READMEs, and provide environment specs or containers for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent replication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Independently replicated evidence is favored over single lab results; independent replication should be planned when feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe who will perform replication and how independence from the discovery team will be ensured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative interpretation and clear limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Honest acknowledgment of limitations and conservative interpretation of results is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list limitations, potential biases, and the boundary conditions for generalizability; avoid overstating conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid single-ancestry studies without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-population studies are penalized unless a clear, justified rationale exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If single-ancestry study is proposed, provide strong justification and plan for subsequent validation in diverse groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mega-consortia without clear PI accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Large consortia lacking clear accountability are criticized; leadership and responsibilities must be explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline governance, PI responsibilities, data stewardship, and publication/attribution policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer clinical impact metrics over citation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate work by clinical impact and patient benefit rather than solely by citation metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame expected patient outcomes, implementation potential, and downstream health benefits in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address funding equity (racial gap and concentration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topol advocates addressing racial gaps in funding and reducing concentration of awards in top institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and institutional plans should demonstrate inclusive practices and capacity building; funders should consider equity in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about industry-academia boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry-academic collaborations are acceptable but require transparency, editorial firewalls, and independent replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the nature of industry involvement, data access, analytic independence, and steps taken to prevent undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slower, more careful peer review for high-stakes work
rubrics_metrics.description: Topol recommends slower, more careful peer review to ensure quality for high-stakes findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For high-impact claims, emphasize rigorous review plans, prepublication validation, and openness to post-publication critique.
